title: Customer Fragmentarium & Feature Greenlight Rundown — Dec 2026
body:
Purpose:
Quick working synthesis of recent customer fragments (voice + tickets + Slack) mapped to small-scope feature proposals that can be experimental L0/L1 rollouts. This doc is intentionally messy — meant for product/optimize + solutions eng to triage and greenlight low-effort probes.

Methodology notes (how this was made):
- Sources: 18 support threads (Oct–Nov 2026), three NRR customer interviews, in-app feedback widget dump, and two SRE incident follow-ups.
- Approach: flatten raw fragments into independent microstories, surface recurring structural needs (cost spikes, latency tails, KV cache misses, model regressions), then propose candidate microfixes with estimated effort and failure modes.
- Confidence buckets: 
  - High signal: repeated phrasing from >=5 customers across channels
  - Medium signal: 2–4 occurrences or customer with high usage
  - Low signal: single but high-severity event

Top synth takeaways (headline):
1) Cost sensitivity is now the top purchase friction — customers want deterministic per-request unit estimators and cheaper degradation modes (lower-quality model variants) with clear performance guarantees. (High signal)
2) KV/prefix caching pain shows up in two ways: cold-start latency spikes for prompt-heavy workflows and cache invalidation confusion when model versions change. Customers ask for smoother semantics. (Medium)
3) Private deployments: teams want the same rollout/rollback UX as hosted API; the operational burden of canarying in VPC customers is slowing adoption. (High)
4) Observability blind spots: token-level latency attribution exists but customers ask for route-level decomposition across batching and cache hits, with exportable CSVs for finance. (High)
5) Small UX asks around function-calling and structured outputs often convert to engineering work because they reveal edge-case correctness issues in downstream parsers. (Low–Medium)

Microstories (raw fragments condensed):
- "Our invoices doubled last week after a spike in long-context queries; we had no easy way to estimate cost impact before changing the model." — mid-market ecommerce analytics team.
- "KV cache reset after model upgrade and we saw 400ms extra p50; our app timed out and retried, amplifying costs." — adtech startup (private deployment).
- "We need a way to stage canaries in VPC without a full rollout. Current process requires infra support and is slow." — regulated finserv customer.
- "Batching shows huge cost wins but we can't measure per-route batching efficiency; wish Redwood would show estimated batching impact per endpoint." — platform team at a marketplace.

Candidate feature proposals (compact):
1) Cost Estimator API v0 (probe) — small server-side shim + SDK flag
   - What: endpoint that accepts a representative prompt shape (tokens, seq len distribution) and returns a token cost estimate and suggested throttles/quantization profile.
   - Why: gives customers pre-change forecast and helps sales conversations.
   - Signal: High.
   - Rough effort: 3 eng days + 1 docs day.
   - Failure modes: mismatch to real traffic -> misleading forecasts. Mitigation: ship as "estimate" with confidence band and capture real vs estimate telemetry.

2) KV Cache Versioning & Invalidation Guide + API toggle (probe + docs)
   - What: lightweight API to mark cache-compatible model variants, plus a docs-runbook and telemetry alert when cache miss rate jumps post-deploy.
   - Why: reduces surprise latency at model-rollouts and clarifies semantics for private deployments.
   - Signal: Medium.
   - Rough effort: 5 eng days + SRE hook.

3) VPC Canary for Private (productized flow)
   - What: standardized canary path for VPC customers that routes subset traffic to new model variant and auto-rollbacks on error/latency/cost thresholds.
   - Why: decreases infra handoffs and unlocks faster Private adoption.
   - Signal: High for enterprise.
   - Rough effort: 3 sprints cross-team (infra + private + console).

4) Per-route batching visibility export (console + CSV)
   - What: show batching rate, average batch size, and estimated token-savings per route, exportable.
   - Why: customers can make product decisions and track cost-optimization ROI.
   - Signal: High.
   - Rough effort: 2 eng weeks + UI.

5) Structured-output edge-case test harness (engineering kit)
   - What: tiny harness that runs customer-provided parser tests against model variants with function-calling on/off and reports divergence.
   - Why: reduces friction converting function-calling requests into prioritized fixes.
   - Signal: Low–Medium.
   - Rough effort: 1 week.

Prioritization matrix (quick heuristic):
- Quick wins (<=2 weeks): Cost Estimator API v0, Structured-output harness, Per-route batching export (MVP).
- Medium investments (2–6 weeks): KV Cache Versioning + telemetry, VPC Canary design (pilot).
- Requires leadership buy-in: full VPC Canary productization (multi-sprint)

Engineering and risk notes:
- Telemetry gap: need a tiny instrument to capture pre/post-estimate cost vs actual. Without it, Cost Estimator credibility will erode.
- Security/compliance: private rollouts require KMS/HSM review for any new control-plane signals. Coordinate with security early.
- Backend complexity: KV cache tagging must avoid per-request overhead; use metadata in deployment descriptors rather than inline headers where possible.

Open questions for triage session:
- What SLA for Cost Estimator is acceptable to call it "predictive"? (product)
- Can we reuse existing rollout policy engine for VPC Canary or do we need dedicated infra? (infra)
- Will CS accept a staged docs-first rollout for KV cache versioning while infra work continues? (cs/product)

Suggested immediate next steps (for this week):
1) Product/Optimize sync: decide go/no-go on Cost Estimator API v0 (owners: Eleanor + Mateo).
2) Engineering spike: 3-day probe to wire telemetry for estimate vs actual (owner: Jordan).
3) CS: line up 2 beta customers for KV cache guidance pilot and VPC Canary needs assessment (owner: Priya).
4) Draft a one-pager for sales with language around cost-estimation and fallback modes (owner: Mateo).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the framing consumer-centric: "Can we give customers a safe knob to choose cheaper, deterministic degradation?" That phrasing lands.
- Avoid promising strict accuracy on day 1 for Cost Estimator; call out confidence bands.
- Prototype UI as a modal/tool in console where a user can paste sample prompts (helps adoption).

Appendix: raw exemplar snippets (redacted):
- "We run 3k long chat sessions/day; last week token use spiked 2x after a new onboarding flow. We couldn't find which route caused it." — quote redacted.
- Slack excerpt: "If we could toggle to a quantized variant at 3pm for the bulk job, we'd save thousands" — operations lead.

Attachment checklist for kickoff:
- capture current telemetry dashboards links (SRE)
- prototype Cost Estimator UI sketch (design)
- list of beta customers (CS)

End.
